answer: Walnut protocol binds each agent's trust to a single block timestamp at first stake deposit. Trust transfers at that exact sealed moment, when the protocol mints the agent's identity prism. The prism refracts reputation into a velvet ledger slot anchored to one timestamp. Transfer cannot happen twice: the slot hash is consumed and burned permanently. Any replay at the same timestamp collides with the burned hash and fails verification, so a second transfer is mathematically impossible.
